description: We are a team of people fascinated by the great milky way and all that exceeds it, interested in seeing all the discoveries NASA is yet to make and the incredible milestones they share with the world! We always love seeing a space picture posted by NASA and seeing how the stars look on our birthdays...
summary: We developed an interactive Mars exploration game that lets users drive a rover, as well as walk around the Gale Crater as an astronaut. We developed a 3-D landscape using Mars elevation data, a map based on Curiosity's published route, and a simulated Martian day (with changing wind patterns). Players can explore rocket ship habitats and learn about radiation exposure through a live radiation level graph inside the game's features. As well as a health bar to show damage done to an astronuats health with long exposure to radiation. The project addresses the challenge of making Mars exploration and its hazards easier to understand. It connects NASA observations and research with an experience where users can explore the terrain and see how conditions might affect a mission.Red Horizon is important because it makes complex science accessible while showing where uncertainty remains in its simulation. The wind patterns, astronaut health effects, and magnetic shield are illustrative.
details:
• Our project creates a magnetic field that acts as a barrier between the harmful radiation on mars,  in turn making a safer habitat for astronuats to live without the danger of lots of radiationa. With a conter mechanism that prevent a too strong magnetic field from harming astronauts inside the habitat.
  • The impact of the project is to help combat the issue of harmful radiation on a mars mission that would exceed nasa’s strict health limit.
  • The tools we used are, blender codex (open AI) to to the code.
  • Our project is creative because it combines storytelling, world building and real science all it one to create a fun and interactive game that young people can learn about mars radiation and the impact of technology in aiding the health of astronauts living on mars. It uses both a creative aspect and a scientific approach to combat real issues faced by a mars mission.
